title: Firehall Meal Prep Ideas
subtitle: Cook once on a slow day — feed the loud ones
description: Firehall meal prep ideas: batch chili, sheet-pan components, pulled pork, and rice bases that reheat clean on busy shifts.
intro: Meal prep at a station means cooking components when the board is quiet so busy nights are assembly, not invention. Firehall meal prep ideas focus on proteins and sauces that reheat — not pre-plated meals that dry out. Below: what halls actually cook for firehall meal prep — formats, timing, and recipe picks that survive a busy board.

sections.heading: Components that reheat clean
paragraphs: Chili, pulled pork, roasted chicken thighs, cooked rice, roasted veg. Combine into bowls, tacos, or bakes in under thirty minutes.
On shift, write the hold plan on the whiteboard — covered on low, finish sear when you're back — so the next cook is not guessing at your flat-top settings.
tips: Assign one cook and one runner; keep everyone else out of the kitchen until called.
Label allergens on the line once — it stops the mid-meal Q&A loop.

sections.heading: Label and rotate
paragraphs: Date everything, freeze what you will not use in three days, and post a fridge map so the next shift does not duplicate prep.
On shift, write the hold plan on the whiteboard — covered on low, finish sear when you're back — so the next cook is not guessing at your flat-top settings.
tips: Assign one cook and one runner; keep everyone else out of the kitchen until called.
Label allergens on the line once — it stops the mid-meal Q&A loop.

sections.heading: Pick the format before the recipe
paragraphs: For firehall meal prep, decide line vs. plated vs. batch before you open a recipe tab. Lines win when eaters show up between 17:00 and 20:00; batches win when you know the whole crew lands at once.
Post protein, starch, and hold plan on the whiteboard. When tones drop, the next cook should read "covered on low" instead of guessing what you meant on the flat-top.
tips: Assign one cook and one runner — everyone else stays out until called.
Sauces on the side keep reheat from turning gluey for post-call eaters.

practicalAdvice: Prep proteins and sauces — assemble day-of.
Date and label everything — rotation prevents science experiments.
One prep cook, one list — avoid three people 'helping' differently.
Post who's cooking and what's holding warm on the whiteboard — post-call eaters should not hunt for answers.
